---
title: "Mediator"
---

The **Mediator** pattern defines an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact. Instead of objects communicating directly (creating a tangled web of dependencies), they communicate through a central mediator — like a smart home hub where devices only know the hub, not each other.

## Problem

Imagine you're building a smart home system. You have lights, thermostats, and motion sensors. The naive approach has each device directly reference and control other devices.

This leads to:

- Devices tightly coupled to each other
- Adding a new device requires modifying existing devices
- Complex N-to-N dependencies (every device potentially knows every other)
- Difficult to reuse devices in different configurations

### Example

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    L[Light] <--> T[Thermostat]
    L <--> M[MotionSensor]
    T <--> M

    style L fill:#fcc,stroke:#c33
    style T fill:#fcc,stroke:#c33
    style M fill:#fcc,stroke:#c33
```

**Problems with this approach:**

- Every device must know about every other device
- Light needs references to MotionSensor and Thermostat
- Adding a new device (e.g., SecurityCamera) means modifying all existing devices
- Testing any device requires mocking all its dependencies

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
class Light:
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
        self.is_on = False
        self.motion_sensor: "MotionSensor | None" = None  # Direct coupling!
        self.thermostat: "Thermostat | None" = None       # More coupling!

    def turn_on(self) -> None:
        self.is_on = True
        print(f"{self.name}: Light turned ON")
        # Directly manipulates thermostat when light turns on
        if self.thermostat:
            self.thermostat.adjust_for_occupancy()

    def turn_off(self) -> None:
        self.is_on = False
        print(f"{self.name}: Light turned OFF")

class MotionSensor:
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
        self.light: "Light | None" = None  # Direct coupling!

    def detect_motion(self) -> None:
        print(f"{self.name}: Motion detected!")
        # Directly controls the light
        if self.light:
            self.light.turn_on()

class Thermostat:
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
        self.temperature = 20

    def adjust_for_occupancy(self) -> None:
        self.temperature = 22
        print(f"{self.name}: Adjusted to {self.temperature}°C for occupancy")
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
public class Light
{
    public string Name { get; }
    public bool IsOn { get; private set; }
    public MotionSensor? MotionSensor { get; set; }  // Direct coupling!
    public Thermostat? Thermostat { get; set; }       // More coupling!

    public Light(string name) => Name = name;

    public void TurnOn()
    {
        IsOn = true;
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Light turned ON");
        // Directly manipulates thermostat when light turns on
        Thermostat?.AdjustForOccupancy();
    }

    public void TurnOff()
    {
        IsOn = false;
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Light turned OFF");
    }
}

public class MotionSensor
{
    public string Name { get; }
    public Light? Light { get; set; }  // Direct coupling!

    public MotionSensor(string name) => Name = name;

    public void DetectMotion()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Motion detected!");
        // Directly controls the light
        Light?.TurnOn();
    }
}

public class Thermostat
{
    public string Name { get; }
    public int Temperature { get; private set; } = 20;

    public Thermostat(string name) => Name = name;

    public void AdjustForOccupancy()
    {
        Temperature = 22;
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Adjusted to {Temperature}°C for occupancy");
    }
}
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::rc::Rc;

struct Light {
    name: String,
    is_on: bool,
    motion_sensor: Option<Rc<RefCell<MotionSensor>>>, // Direct coupling!
    thermostat: Option<Rc<RefCell<Thermostat>>>,      // More coupling!
}

impl Light {
    fn new(name: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            is_on: false,
            motion_sensor: None,
            thermostat: None,
        }
    }

    fn turn_on(&mut self) {
        self.is_on = true;
        println!("{}: Light turned ON", self.name);
        // Directly manipulates thermostat when light turns on
        if let Some(thermostat) = &self.thermostat {
            thermostat.borrow_mut().adjust_for_occupancy();
        }
    }

    fn turn_off(&mut self) {
        self.is_on = false;
        println!("{}: Light turned OFF", self.name);
    }
}

struct MotionSensor {
    name: String,
    light: Option<Rc<RefCell<Light>>>, // Direct coupling!
}

impl MotionSensor {
    fn new(name: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            light: None,
        }
    }

    fn detect_motion(&self) {
        println!("{}: Motion detected!", self.name);
        // Directly controls the light
        if let Some(light) = &self.light {
            light.borrow_mut().turn_on();
        }
    }
}

struct Thermostat {
    name: String,
    temperature: i32,
}

impl Thermostat {
    fn new(name: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            temperature: 20,
        }
    }

    fn adjust_for_occupancy(&mut self) {
        self.temperature = 22;
        println!(
            "{}: Adjusted to {}°C for occupancy",
            self.name, self.temperature
        );
    }
}
```

#### Usage

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Must wire up all the connections manually
light = Light("Living Room Light")
sensor = MotionSensor("Entry Sensor")
thermostat = Thermostat("Main Thermostat")

# Every device must know about every other device!
sensor.light = light
light.thermostat = thermostat

sensor.detect_motion()
# Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
# Living Room Light: Light turned ON
# Main Thermostat: Adjusted to 22°C for occupancy

# What if we add a SecurityCamera? Must modify Light, Sensor, etc.!
```

```rust
fn main() {
    // Must wire up all the connections manually,
    // and every shared device needs Rc<RefCell<…>>
    let light = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Light::new("Living Room Light")));
    let mut sensor = MotionSensor::new("Entry Sensor");
    let thermostat = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Thermostat::new("Main Thermostat")));

    // Every device must know about every other device!
    sensor.light = Some(Rc::clone(&light));
    light.borrow_mut().thermostat = Some(Rc::clone(&thermostat));

    sensor.detect_motion();
    // Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
    // Living Room Light: Light turned ON
    // Main Thermostat: Adjusted to 22°C for occupancy

    // What if we add a SecurityCamera? Must modify Light, Sensor, etc.!
}
```

## Solution

The Mediator pattern solves this by:

1. Introducing a **mediator** (`SmartHomeHub`) that coordinates device interactions
2. Each **colleague** (`SmartDevice`) only knows the mediator, not other devices
3. When something happens, devices notify the hub, which orchestrates the response
4. All coordination logic is centralized in the mediator

The result: N-to-N relationships become N-to-1, and devices are completely decoupled.

### UML Diagram

```{mermaid}
classDiagram
    class SmartHomeHub {
        -devices: List~SmartDevice~
        +register(device: SmartDevice)
        +notify(sender: SmartDevice, event: String)
    }

    class SmartDevice {
        <<abstract>>
        #hub: SmartHomeHub
        #name: String
        +notifyHub(event: String)
    }

    class Light {
        -isOn: bool
        +turnOn()
        +turnOff()
    }

    class Thermostat {
        -temperature: int
        +setTemperature(temp: int)
    }

    class MotionSensor {
        +detectMotion()
    }

    SmartDevice <|-- Light
    SmartDevice <|-- Thermostat
    SmartDevice <|-- MotionSensor
    SmartDevice --> SmartHomeHub : notifies
    SmartHomeHub --> SmartDevice : coordinates
```

### Refactored Code

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
from abc import ABC

# Mediator
class SmartHomeHub:
    def __init__(self):
        self._devices: dict[str, "SmartDevice"] = {}

    def register(self, device: "SmartDevice") -> None:
        self._devices[device.name] = device
        device._hub = self
        print(f"Hub: Registered {device.name}")

    def notify(self, sender: "SmartDevice", event: str) -> None:
        print(f"Hub: Received '{event}' from {sender.name}")

        # Coordination logic centralized here!
        if event == "motion_detected":
            # Turn on lights when motion detected
            for device in self._devices.values():
                if isinstance(device, Light):
                    device.turn_on()

        elif event == "light_on":
            # Adjust thermostat when light turns on (room occupied)
            for device in self._devices.values():
                if isinstance(device, Thermostat):
                    device.set_temperature(22)

# Abstract Colleague
class SmartDevice(ABC):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
        self._hub: SmartHomeHub | None = None

    def notify_hub(self, event: str) -> None:
        if self._hub:
            self._hub.notify(self, event)

# Concrete Colleagues
class Light(SmartDevice):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.is_on = False

    def turn_on(self) -> None:
        self.is_on = True
        print(f"{self.name}: Light turned ON")
        self.notify_hub("light_on")

    def turn_off(self) -> None:
        self.is_on = False
        print(f"{self.name}: Light turned OFF")
        self.notify_hub("light_off")

class Thermostat(SmartDevice):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.temperature = 20

    def set_temperature(self, temp: int) -> None:
        self.temperature = temp
        print(f"{self.name}: Temperature set to {temp}°C")

class MotionSensor(SmartDevice):
    def detect_motion(self) -> None:
        print(f"{self.name}: Motion detected!")
        self.notify_hub("motion_detected")
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
// Mediator
public class SmartHomeHub
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, SmartDevice> _devices = new();

    public void Register(SmartDevice device)
    {
        _devices[device.Name] = device;
        device.Hub = this;
        Console.WriteLine($"Hub: Registered {device.Name}");
    }

    public void Notify(SmartDevice sender, string eventType)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Hub: Received '{eventType}' from {sender.Name}");

        // Coordination logic centralized here!
        if (eventType == "motion_detected")
        {
            // Turn on lights when motion detected
            foreach (var device in _devices.Values)
            {
                if (device is Light light)
                    light.TurnOn();
            }
        }
        else if (eventType == "light_on")
        {
            // Adjust thermostat when light turns on (room occupied)
            foreach (var device in _devices.Values)
            {
                if (device is Thermostat thermostat)
                    thermostat.SetTemperature(22);
            }
        }
    }
}

// Abstract Colleague
public abstract class SmartDevice
{
    public string Name { get; }
    public SmartHomeHub? Hub { get; set; }

    protected SmartDevice(string name) => Name = name;

    protected void NotifyHub(string eventType) => Hub?.Notify(this, eventType);
}

// Concrete Colleagues
public class Light : SmartDevice
{
    public bool IsOn { get; private set; }

    public Light(string name) : base(name) { }

    public void TurnOn()
    {
        IsOn = true;
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Light turned ON");
        NotifyHub("light_on");
    }

    public void TurnOff()
    {
        IsOn = false;
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Light turned OFF");
        NotifyHub("light_off");
    }
}

public class Thermostat : SmartDevice
{
    public int Temperature { get; private set; } = 20;

    public Thermostat(string name) : base(name) { }

    public void SetTemperature(int temp)
    {
        Temperature = temp;
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Temperature set to {temp}°C");
    }
}

public class MotionSensor : SmartDevice
{
    public MotionSensor(string name) : base(name) { }

    public void DetectMotion()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{Name}: Motion detected!");
        NotifyHub("motion_detected");
    }
}
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::rc::{Rc, Weak};

// Mediator → shared as Rc<SmartHomeHub>; RefCell lets register() grow the list
struct SmartHomeHub {
    devices: RefCell<Vec<Device>>,
}

// The hub must know concrete device types (Python's isinstance) → an enum of handles
enum Device {
    Light(Rc<RefCell<Light>>),
    Thermostat(Rc<RefCell<Thermostat>>),
    MotionSensor(Rc<RefCell<MotionSensor>>),
}

impl Device {
    fn name(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Device::Light(d) => d.borrow().device.name.clone(),
            Device::Thermostat(d) => d.borrow().device.name.clone(),
            Device::MotionSensor(d) => d.borrow().device.name.clone(),
        }
    }
}

impl SmartHomeHub {
    fn new() -> Rc<Self> {
        Rc::new(Self {
            devices: RefCell::new(Vec::new()),
        })
    }

    fn register(&self, device: Device) {
        println!("Hub: Registered {}", device.name());
        self.devices.borrow_mut().push(device);
    }

    fn notify(&self, sender: &str, event: &str) {
        println!("Hub: Received '{event}' from {sender}");

        // Coordination logic centralized here!
        for device in self.devices.borrow().iter() {
            match (event, device) {
                // Turn on lights when motion detected
                ("motion_detected", Device::Light(light)) => light.borrow_mut().turn_on(),
                // Adjust thermostat when light turns on (room occupied)
                ("light_on", Device::Thermostat(thermostat)) => {
                    thermostat.borrow_mut().set_temperature(22)
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
}

// Abstract colleague → a struct every device embeds (composition, not inheritance)
struct SmartDevice {
    name: String,
    hub: Weak<SmartHomeHub>, // Weak: the hub owns the devices, so a strong Rc would be a cycle
}

impl SmartDevice {
    fn new(name: &str, hub: &Rc<SmartHomeHub>) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            hub: Rc::downgrade(hub),
        }
    }

    fn notify_hub(&self, event: &str) {
        if let Some(hub) = self.hub.upgrade() {
            hub.notify(&self.name, event);
        }
    }
}

// Concrete colleagues
struct Light {
    device: SmartDevice,
    is_on: bool,
}

impl Light {
    fn new(name: &str, hub: &Rc<SmartHomeHub>) -> Self {
        Self {
            device: SmartDevice::new(name, hub),
            is_on: false,
        }
    }

    fn turn_on(&mut self) {
        self.is_on = true;
        println!("{}: Light turned ON", self.device.name);
        self.device.notify_hub("light_on");
    }

    fn turn_off(&mut self) {
        self.is_on = false;
        println!("{}: Light turned OFF", self.device.name);
        self.device.notify_hub("light_off");
    }
}

struct Thermostat {
    device: SmartDevice,
    temperature: i32,
}

impl Thermostat {
    fn new(name: &str, hub: &Rc<SmartHomeHub>) -> Self {
        Self {
            device: SmartDevice::new(name, hub),
            temperature: 20,
        }
    }

    fn set_temperature(&mut self, temp: i32) {
        self.temperature = temp;
        println!("{}: Temperature set to {temp}°C", self.device.name);
    }
}

struct MotionSensor {
    device: SmartDevice,
}

impl MotionSensor {
    fn new(name: &str, hub: &Rc<SmartHomeHub>) -> Self {
        Self {
            device: SmartDevice::new(name, hub),
        }
    }

    fn detect_motion(&self) {
        println!("{}: Motion detected!", self.device.name);
        self.device.notify_hub("motion_detected");
    }
}
```

#### Usage

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Create the hub (mediator)
hub = SmartHomeHub()

# Create devices — they don't know about each other!
light = Light("Living Room Light")
thermostat = Thermostat("Main Thermostat")
sensor = MotionSensor("Entry Sensor")

# Register all devices with the hub
hub.register(light)
hub.register(thermostat)
hub.register(sensor)

# Hub: Registered Living Room Light
# Hub: Registered Main Thermostat
# Hub: Registered Entry Sensor

print("\n--- Motion Detected ---")
sensor.detect_motion()

# Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
# Hub: Received 'motion_detected' from Entry Sensor
# Living Room Light: Light turned ON
# Hub: Received 'light_on' from Living Room Light
# Main Thermostat: Temperature set to 22°C

# Adding new devices? Just register with hub — no changes to existing devices!
```

```rust
fn main() {
    // Create the hub (mediator)
    let hub = SmartHomeHub::new();

    // Create devices — they know only the hub, not each other!
    let light = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Light::new("Living Room Light", &hub)));
    let thermostat = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Thermostat::new("Main Thermostat", &hub)));
    let sensor = Rc::new(RefCell::new(MotionSensor::new("Entry Sensor", &hub)));

    // Register all devices with the hub
    hub.register(Device::Light(Rc::clone(&light)));
    hub.register(Device::Thermostat(Rc::clone(&thermostat)));
    hub.register(Device::MotionSensor(Rc::clone(&sensor)));

    // Hub: Registered Living Room Light
    // Hub: Registered Main Thermostat
    // Hub: Registered Entry Sensor

    println!("\n--- Motion Detected ---");
    sensor.borrow().detect_motion();

    // Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
    // Hub: Received 'motion_detected' from Entry Sensor
    // Living Room Light: Light turned ON
```

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="🦀 Rust lens"}
| GoF role | Rust |
|---|---|
| Mediator | `SmartHomeHub`, shared as `Rc<SmartHomeHub>` |
| Abstract colleague | a `SmartDevice` struct (name + hub) that every device embeds: composition, no base class |
| Colleague → mediator reference | `Weak<SmartHomeHub>`, upgraded to an `Rc` on each `notify_hub()` |
| Mediator → colleagues | `RefCell<Vec<Device>>`, where `enum Device` holds one `Rc<RefCell<…>>` per device type |
| `isinstance(device, Light)` | `match (event, device)` on the `Device` enum |

**Ownership:** the hub and the devices point at each other. Two `Rc`s in a cycle never reach a count of zero, so the device side holds a `Weak`. The calls also re-enter: the hub calls `light.turn_on()`, which calls `hub.notify()` again before the first call returns. That works because `notify()` takes only shared borrows of the device list. A rule that borrowed the sending light mutably a second time would compile, but `RefCell` would panic at runtime ("already borrowed"). See the [OOP Cheatsheet](../oop/oop-cheatsheet.qmd#rust) for the general mapping.
:::

## Modern Approach

Today the hub is usually a generic **event bus** (publish/subscribe). TypeScript and Dart ship one in the standard library, and C# builds one from multicast delegates. Rust builds one from a `std::sync::mpsc` channel and a map of closures. The channel also breaks the hub ↔ device reference cycle, because a device holds only a `Sender`. Devices only publish named events, and they need no base class or hub reference. The catch is that an event bus is a *mediator without the brain*. The coordination rules (motion → light on → thermostat) don't disappear. They move into the subscriptions, so give them one clearly named home.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Verdict: 🟡 Simplifies** — a generic event bus replaces the hand-written hub and the colleague base class, but the coordination rules still need a home.
:::

### Feature Map

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class SmartHomeHub` with `register()` / `notify()` | `EventBus` with `subscribe()` / `publish()` over a `defaultdict(list)` of callables |
| `if event == …` + `isinstance(device, Light)` inside the hub | subscriptions: `bus.subscribe("motion_detected", lambda _: light.turn_on())` |
| `class SmartDevice(ABC)` with a `_hub` back-reference | plain classes that receive a `publish` function |
| `hub.register(device)` | none: devices only need `publish` |
| `self.notify_hub("light_on")` | `self._publish("light_on", self.name)` |

#### `C#`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class SmartHomeHub` with `Register()` / `Notify()` | `EventBus` holding one multicast `Action<string>` per event name |
| `if (eventType == …)` + `device is Light` inside the hub | subscriptions: `bus.Subscribe("motion_detected", _ => light.TurnOn())` |
| `abstract class SmartDevice` with a `Hub` property | primary-constructor classes taking an `Action<string, string> publish` |
| `hub.Register(device)` | none: devices only need `publish` |
| `NotifyHub("light_on")` | `publish("light_on", name)` |

#### `TypeScript`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class SmartHomeHub` with `register()` / `notify()` | built-in `EventTarget` + `CustomEvent` (subclassed to log each event) |
| `if (event === …)` + `instanceof Light` inside the hub | listeners: `bus.addEventListener("motion_detected", () => light.turnOn())` |
| `abstract class SmartDevice` with a `hub` field | plain classes that receive a `publish` function |
| `hub.register(device)` | none: devices only need `publish` |
| `this.notifyHub("light_on")` | `this.publish("light_on", this.name)` |

#### `Dart`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class SmartHomeHub` with `register()` / `notify()` | `StreamController.broadcast()` (`dart:async`) wrapped in a small `EventBus` |
| `if (event == …)` + `device is Light` inside the hub | subscriptions: `bus.subscribe("motion_detected", (_) => light.turnOn())` |
| `abstract class SmartDevice` with a `_hub` field | plain classes that receive a `Publish` function |
| `hub.register(device)` | none: devices only need `publish` |
| synchronous `notify()` call | stream listeners run as microtasks, after the current code finishes |

#### `Rust`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `struct SmartHomeHub` with `register()` / `notify()` | `EventBus` with `subscribe()`, a `publisher()` channel, and `run()` |
| `match (event, device)` over an enum of device handles | subscriptions: a `move` closure that owns the light, registered for `Event::MotionDetected` |
| `SmartDevice` struct with a `Weak<SmartHomeHub>` back-reference | a cloned `mpsc::Sender`: the device can only send, never reach the bus |
| `Rc<RefCell<…>>` around every device | each handler closure owns its device: no `Rc`, no `RefCell` |
| String events (`"light_on"`) | `enum Event`: a misspelled event is a compile error |
| Nested calls: hub → light → hub again | `run()` drains a queue, so a handler never re-enters the bus |

:::

**Ecosystem:** .NET has MediatR (moved to a commercial license in 2025) and CommunityToolkit.Mvvm's `IMessenger` for UI apps. Python has `blinker`, TypeScript has RxJS `Subject`, and Dart has `event_bus` and Bloc. In Rust, `tokio::sync::broadcast` channels and actor frameworks such as `actix` play the bus role. Across services, the same idea scales up to a message broker (RabbitMQ, Kafka).

### Modern Code

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Python 3.12+ — callables in a defaultdict(list) as a tiny event bus
from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import Callable

type Handler = Callable[[str], None]  # receives the sender's name
type Publish = Callable[[str, str], None]  # (event, sender)


# Mediator → a generic event bus: it routes events but knows no device types
class EventBus:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._handlers: defaultdict[str, list[Handler]] = defaultdict(list)

    def subscribe(self, event: str, handler: Handler) -> None:
        self._handlers[event].append(handler)

    def publish(self, event: str, sender: str) -> None:
        print(f"Bus: '{event}' from {sender}")
        for handler in self._handlers[event]:
            handler(sender)


# Colleagues → no base class, no hub reference: each gets a `publish` function
class Light:
    def __init__(self, name: str, publish: Publish) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self._publish = publish
        self.is_on = False

    def turn_on(self) -> None:
        self.is_on = True
        print(f"{self.name}: Light turned ON")
        self._publish("light_on", self.name)


class Thermostat:
    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.temperature = 20

    def set_temperature(self, temp: int) -> None:
        self.temperature = temp
        print(f"{self.name}: Temperature set to {temp}°C")


class MotionSensor:
    def __init__(self, name: str, publish: Publish) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self._publish = publish

    def detect_motion(self) -> None:
        print(f"{self.name}: Motion detected!")
        self._publish("motion_detected", self.name)


# --- Usage ---
bus = EventBus()
light = Light("Living Room Light", bus.publish)
thermostat = Thermostat("Main Thermostat")
sensor = MotionSensor("Entry Sensor", bus.publish)

# The coordination rules ("the brain") now live in the wiring
bus.subscribe("motion_detected", lambda _: light.turn_on())
bus.subscribe("light_on", lambda _: thermostat.set_temperature(22))

print("--- Motion Detected ---")
sensor.detect_motion()
# --- Motion Detected ---
# Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
# Bus: 'motion_detected' from Entry Sensor
# Living Room Light: Light turned ON
# Bus: 'light_on' from Living Room Light
# Main Thermostat: Temperature set to 22°C
```

```csharp
// C# 12 / .NET 8+ — multicast delegates (Action<T>), lambdas, primary constructors

// Mediator → a generic event bus: it routes events but knows no device types
public class EventBus
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, Action<string>> _handlers = [];

    // `+` combines delegates: one Action can call many handlers
    public void Subscribe(string eventName, Action<string> handler) =>
        _handlers[eventName] = _handlers.GetValueOrDefault(eventName) + handler;

    public void Publish(string eventName, string sender)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Bus: '{eventName}' from {sender}");
        _handlers.GetValueOrDefault(eventName)?.Invoke(sender);
    }
}

// Colleagues → no base class, no hub reference: each gets a `publish` delegate
public class Light(string name, Action<string, string> publish)
{
    public bool IsOn { get; private set; }

    public void TurnOn()
    {
        IsOn = true;
        Console.WriteLine($"{name}: Light turned ON");
        publish("light_on", name);
    }
}

public class Thermostat(string name)
{
    public int Temperature { get; private set; } = 20;

    public void SetTemperature(int temp)
    {
        Temperature = temp;
        Console.WriteLine($"{name}: Temperature set to {temp}°C");
    }
}

public class MotionSensor(string name, Action<string, string> publish)
{
    public void DetectMotion()
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{name}: Motion detected!");
        publish("motion_detected", name);
    }
}

// --- Usage ---
var bus = new EventBus();
var light = new Light("Living Room Light", bus.Publish);
var thermostat = new Thermostat("Main Thermostat");
var sensor = new MotionSensor("Entry Sensor", bus.Publish);

// The coordination rules ("the brain") now live in the wiring
bus.Subscribe("motion_detected", _ => light.TurnOn());
bus.Subscribe("light_on", _ => thermostat.SetTemperature(22));

Console.WriteLine("--- Motion Detected ---");
sensor.DetectMotion();
// --- Motion Detected ---
// Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
// Bus: 'motion_detected' from Entry Sensor
// Living Room Light: Light turned ON
// Bus: 'light_on' from Living Room Light
// Main Thermostat: Temperature set to 22°C
```

```dart
// Dart 3.x — StreamController.broadcast (dart:async) as the event bus, records
import 'dart:async';

typedef Publish = void Function(String type, String sender);

// Mediator → a broadcast stream: it routes events but knows no device types
class EventBus {
  final _events = StreamController<({String type, String sender})>.broadcast();

  void publish(String type, String sender) {
    print("Bus: '$type' from $sender");
    _events.add((type: type, sender: sender));
  }

  void subscribe(String type, void Function(String sender) handler) {
    _events.stream.where((e) => e.type == type).listen((e) => handler(e.sender));
  }
}

// Colleagues → no base class, no hub reference: each gets a `publish` function
class Light {
  final String name;
  final Publish _publish;
  bool isOn = false;

  Light(this.name, this._publish);

  void turnOn() {
    isOn = true;
    print("$name: Light turned ON");
    _publish("light_on", name);
  }
}

class Thermostat {
  final String name;
  int temperature = 20;

  Thermostat(this.name);

  void setTemperature(int temp) {
    temperature = temp;
    print("$name: Temperature set to $temp°C");
  }
}

class MotionSensor {
  final String name;
  final Publish _publish;

  MotionSensor(this.name, this._publish);

  void detectMotion() {
    print("$name: Motion detected!");
    _publish("motion_detected", name);
  }
}

// --- Usage ---
void main() {
  final bus = EventBus();
  final light = Light("Living Room Light", bus.publish);
  final thermostat = Thermostat("Main Thermostat");
  final sensor = MotionSensor("Entry Sensor", bus.publish);

  // The coordination rules ("the brain") now live in the wiring
  bus.subscribe("motion_detected", (_) => light.turnOn());
  bus.subscribe("light_on", (_) => thermostat.setTemperature(22));

  print("--- Motion Detected ---");
  sensor.detectMotion();
  // Stream listeners run as microtasks, right after main's synchronous code:
  // --- Motion Detected ---
  // Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
  // Bus: 'motion_detected' from Entry Sensor
  // Living Room Light: Light turned ON
  // Bus: 'light_on' from Living Room Light
  // Main Thermostat: Temperature set to 22°C
}
```

#### `Rust`

```rust
// Rust 1.85+ (edition 2024) — std::sync::mpsc channel + enum events + boxed closures
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::mpsc::{self, Receiver, Sender};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum Event {
    MotionDetected,
    LightOn,
}

impl Event {
    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Event::MotionDetected => "motion_detected",
            Event::LightOn => "light_on",
        }
    }
}

type Handler = Box<dyn FnMut(&str)>; // receives the sender's name
type Publish = Sender<(Event, String)>; // (event, sender)

// Mediator → a generic event bus: it routes events but knows no device types
struct EventBus {
    handlers: HashMap<Event, Vec<Handler>>,
    publish: Publish,
    inbox: Receiver<(Event, String)>,
}

impl EventBus {
    fn new() -> Self {
        let (publish, inbox) = mpsc::channel();
        Self {
            handlers: HashMap::new(),
            publish,
            inbox,
        }
    }

    // Each colleague gets its own cloned Sender: no reference back to the bus
    fn publisher(&self) -> Publish {
        self.publish.clone()
    }

    fn subscribe(&mut self, event: Event, handler: impl FnMut(&str) + 'static) {
        self.handlers
            .entry(event)
            .or_default()
            .push(Box::new(handler));
    }

    // Deliver queued events one at a time, so a handler never re-enters the bus
    fn run(&mut self) {
        while let Ok((event, sender)) = self.inbox.try_recv() {
            println!("Bus: '{}' from {sender}", event.name());
            for handler in self.handlers.get_mut(&event).into_iter().flatten() {
                handler(&sender);
            }
        }
    }
}

// Colleagues → no base struct, no hub reference: each holds a `publish` Sender
struct Light {
    name: String,
    publish: Publish,
    is_on: bool,
}

impl Light {
    fn new(name: &str, publish: Publish) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            publish,
            is_on: false,
        }
    }

    fn turn_on(&mut self) {
        if self.is_on {
            return; // already on: nothing to announce
        }
        self.is_on = true;
        println!("{}: Light turned ON", self.name);
        self.publish
            .send((Event::LightOn, self.name.clone()))
            .expect("event bus is alive");
    }
}

struct Thermostat {
    name: String,
    temperature: i32,
}

impl Thermostat {
    fn new(name: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            temperature: 20,
        }
    }

    fn set_temperature(&mut self, temp: i32) {
        self.temperature = temp;
        println!("{}: Temperature set to {}°C", self.name, self.temperature);
    }
}

struct MotionSensor {
    name: String,
    publish: Publish,
}

impl MotionSensor {
    fn new(name: &str, publish: Publish) -> Self {
        Self {
            name: name.to_string(),
            publish,
        }
    }

    fn detect_motion(&self) {
        println!("{}: Motion detected!", self.name);
        self.publish
            .send((Event::MotionDetected, self.name.clone()))
            .expect("event bus is alive");
    }
}

// --- Usage ---
fn main() {
    let mut bus = EventBus::new();
    let mut light = Light::new("Living Room Light", bus.publisher());
    let mut thermostat = Thermostat::new("Main Thermostat");
    let sensor = MotionSensor::new("Entry Sensor", bus.publisher());

    // The coordination rules ("the brain") now live in the wiring.
    // Each handler owns the device it drives: no Rc, no RefCell.
    bus.subscribe(Event::MotionDetected, move |_| light.turn_on());
    bus.subscribe(Event::LightOn, move |_| thermostat.set_temperature(22));

    println!("--- Motion Detected ---");
    sensor.detect_motion();
    bus.run();
    // --- Motion Detected ---
    // Entry Sensor: Motion detected!
    // Bus: 'motion_detected' from Entry Sensor
    // Living Room Light: Light turned ON
    // Bus: 'light_on' from Living Room Light
    // Main Thermostat: Temperature set to 22°C
}
```

:::

### Classic or Modern?

| Prefer an event bus when | Keep a dedicated mediator class when |
|---|---|
| Rules are simple "when X happens, do Y" reactions | A rule depends on several devices' state at once ("lights on only if it's dark and someone is home") |
| Publishers and subscribers should not know each other at all | You want the whole workflow readable, testable, and debuggable in one place |
| Reactions are added often, by different modules or teams | Step ordering, error handling, or rollback across steps matters |
| Rust: reactions are independent, so a queue can deliver them one at a time | Rust: a rule reads or changes several devices at once. A hub that *owns* the devices does that with plain `&mut`, without `Rc` or `RefCell` |

## Summary

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" collapse="false"}
**Mediator** centralizes complex communication between objects, replacing N-to-N dependencies with N-to-1 relationships through a coordinating hub.
:::

### Key Benefits

- **Loose Coupling**: Objects only know the mediator, not each other
- **Centralized Logic**: All coordination rules in one place
- **Easy Extension**: Add new colleagues without modifying existing ones
- **Simplified Objects**: Colleagues focus on their own behavior, not coordination
- **Reusability**: Colleagues can be reused in different configurations

### Real-World Examples

| Application | Mediator |
|-------------|----------|
| **Smart Home** | Hub coordinates devices |
| **Air Traffic Control** | Tower coordinates aircraft |
| **Chat Applications** | Chat room/server routes messages |
| **UI Frameworks** | Dialog/Form coordinates components |
| **Message Brokers** | Kafka/RabbitMQ coordinate services |

### When to Use

| ✅ Use When | ❌ Avoid When |
|------------|--------------|
| Multiple objects communicate in complex ways | Communication between objects is simple |
| Objects have many direct dependencies on each other | There are only 2-3 objects interacting |
| You want to customize interaction behavior in one place | The mediator would become a "god object" with too much logic |
| You need to reuse objects across different coordination rules | Direct coupling is acceptable and simpler |
